From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 25 Aug 2026 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: RE: MSA + Order Form intake: compliance flags, template choice, and redline priority matrix

Karthik / Marissa —

Thanks for the packet. Quick read-through notes and proposed intake plan below. I’ll own the first redline pass and the priority matrix.

Summary of primary legal/compliance flags noticed on initial skim:

1) Liability cap: counterparty has unlimited liability carveouts for certain data breaches — propose to cap at 2x fees for commercial risk and carve criminal/intentional tort exceptions.
2) IP assignment: there are broad customer-originated IP clauses that risk Redwood-owned model outputs; propose clarifying language to preserve model output IP for Redwood while granting customer usage rights.
3) Data residency and export: the MSA references cross-border processing without required safeguards; propose an addendum for EU failover and standard SCCs if EU processing occurs.
4) Subprocessor list / right to audit: add a required notice period for new subprocessors and narrow audit scope to material incidents.

Proposed intake timelines (assuming we start today):
- Template-fit mapping: 1 business day (I’ll map clauses to our template and flag purchase-specific variants)
- Priority matrix & annotated redline (tracked doc): 2 business days
- Internal legal-review sync: 30 minutes on Wednesday after our draft

Questions for Karthik / Carl:
- Confirm whether Atlas insists on 60-day payment term at signature; if so, will push billing to weigh risk/cost.
- Does Atlas expect SOC2 evidence to be bundled at signature or during onboarding? (this affects whether we lock residency language now)

I’ll attach a tracked redline (first pass) to CONTRACT-234 when ready and copy in Emily if any client-side tradeoffs need legal-to-legal discussion.

Kimberly Park
Senior Counsel, Contracts & Privacy
kimberly_park@redwood.ai
